body: More than 16,000 people work on Galfar projects, around 3,500 to 3,900 of them Omani. Galfar is among the three biggest national employers in the private sector.

about.title: A partner in Oman's renaissance since 1972
body: Galfar Engineering & Contracting SAOG was established in 1972 and has grown into one of the largest publicly listed companies in Oman and one of the largest construction companies in the Middle East.

Its work runs through three business units: Energy & Industrial, Infrastructure, and Civil & Environmental, supported by units for QHSSE, project services, human capital, finance and IT, supply chain, and strategy and business development.
more: Galfar has delivered more than 1,000 projects worth over US$10 billion, built over 4,000 km of roads and laid over 8,000 km of pipelines and flowlines. It owns more than 4,000 plant and machines and works with over 1,500 registered local vendors.
With partners, Galfar has also moved into 3D printing for construction.

services.title: Capabilities
services.intro: Three business units deliver the projects. Support units keep people, plant and suppliers moving.

items.title: Energy & Industrial
items.text: Oil and gas, petrochemical and industrial plants, power generation and grids.

detail.intro: This unit covers oil and gas work upstream and downstream, petrochemical, manufacturing and industrial plants, and conventional and green energy projects.
body: With proven upstream service capability in design, civil, mechanical, electrical and instrumentation, the unit has executed the largest contract in the history of Oman, worth more than USD 2 billion.

It handles service contracts from wellhead hook-up up to delivery into gathering stations for Petroleum Development Oman, OQ, BP, Occidental Oman, Daleel and others. Recent work includes the Salalah LPG plant, Duqm Refinery and the Yibal Khuff separation, processing and sulphur recovery plant.

The unit has built oil storage tanks, gathering and compressor stations and enhanced oil recovery projects with DCS and SCADA controls, blast-proof buildings, and power transmission systems from 11 kV to 132 kV. Its team numbers more than 6,000. It was once honoured with the British Safety Council's Sword of Honour.
points: Upstream and downstream oil and gas
Storage tanks, gathering and compressor stations

items.title: Infrastructure
items.text: Roads, bridges, airports, seaports, dams, rail and water networks.

detail.intro: Roads and bridges, airports and seaports, flood protection and recharge dams, railways, water and wastewater networks, and large earthmoving projects, as EPC or construction contracts.
body: Over the last three decades Galfar has built nearly one third of Oman's roads, including the Muscat Expressway, Batinah Expressway packages 1 and 3, the Jebel Al Akhdar road to Saiq, the Bousher–Amerat road and the Hasik–Shuwaymiyah road. These include the highest mechanically stabilised walls and the longest underpass tunnels in Oman.

With its fleet of heavy earthmoving equipment, the unit has handled excavation, backfill and reclamation, such as backfilling for Muscat International Airport and ground levelling for the refinery complex in Duqm. It executed the airside works at Salalah International Airport as a joint venture partner, built airports for PDO, airside facilities at Ras Al Hadd and rehabilitated the old Muscat International Airport.

The unit builds ports and fishing harbours, dams and recharge structures, and water transmission networks, and maintains about 75% of the existing water transmission and distribution network for Oman's water authorities. It has more than 7,000 employees, over 1,100 of them in specialised roles held by Omani nationals.
points: Operation and maintenance of water networks

items.title: Civil & Environmental
items.text: Landmark buildings, MEP, wastewater plants and networks, operation and maintenance.

detail.intro: Galfar's first operating unit builds landmark buildings and MEP services, wastewater treatment plants and networks, and operates and maintains them.
body: Over the years the unit has built palaces, commercial buildings, housing, schools, hospitals, monuments, religious buildings, stadiums, showrooms and residences, large civil works for industrial plants, and several turnkey hotels across Oman.

Early hospitals at Ibri, Nizwa and Sur led to larger projects such as the Salalah Extended Health Centre, the National Heart Centre at the Royal Hospital, an Accident, Emergency and Burns unit and the Salalah Cardiac Centre, followed by operation and maintenance of these facilities. The unit has also built guest complexes, offices, border posts and utility buildings for the Royal Court Affairs and other authorities.

In the environment sector it completed Oman's first membrane bioreactor plant at Al Ansab, the region's largest vacuum sewer network at Seeb, several sewage treatment plants, collection networks and reverse osmosis plants.
points: Operation and maintenance of buildings and networks

items.title: QHSSE
items.text: Quality, health, safety, security and environment, certified to ISO standards.

detail.intro: HSE is a top priority at Galfar: the health and safety of employees and stakeholders, and the protection of the environment.
body: Quality, health, safety, security and environment combine into one management approach that reduces process errors, rework, workplace accidents, occupational illness and environmental impact, and protects project assets.

The QHSSE Systems Unit works with every other unit through risk assessments, corporate QHSSE plans, management system audits, staff competence development, compliance monitoring and management reviews. It runs lean management initiatives, flawless project delivery plans, task workshops and training, campaigns, observation reporting, inspections and incident investigations.

items.title: Project Services
items.text: Fleet, workshops, fabrication, engineering and design for every project.

detail.intro: The Project Services Unit gives Galfar central support: commercial and contract management, fleet and workforce planning, engineering and design, plant and fabrication workshops, and asset use.
body: Galfar runs one of the largest repair and maintenance workshop networks in Oman. Its service workshops include the Nizwa Industrial Facility, a carpentry workshop, a waterproofing and coating complex, and scaffolding and formwork installations, placed across Oman to support projects.

The Nizwa Industrial Facility, established in 2006, serves in-house and third-party clients with structural fabrication, CS/LTCS and SS/DSS/SDSS/alloy piping fabrication, plate rolling, and blasting, coating and painting.

items.title: Careers & Human Capital
items.text: A 16,000-strong, multinational team and a leader in Omanisation.

detail.intro: Galfar is a multidisciplinary, multinational team and one of the largest employers in the region.
body: With a workforce of more than 16,000, around 3,500 of them Omani nationals, Galfar works to provide an environment that encourages excellence.
Its Omanisation programme is one of its proudest achievements: Galfar leads in providing job opportunities to nationals and in training and employing them.
Human Capital attracts, develops and keeps talent, and looks for lateral thinkers with a strong teamwork ethic. Open roles are listed on Galfar's careers portal.

items.title: In-Country Value
items.text: Omani shareholders, Omani staff and a local supply chain.

detail.intro: In-country value is a main goal for Galfar: growing local content through local procurement and developing its workforce.
body: Galfar has been listed on the Muscat Stock Exchange since 2007 and has more than 4,000 shareholders. About 85% of them, individuals and institutions such as local companies and pension funds, are Omani.
Galfar is among the three biggest national employers in Oman's private sector, with about 3,900 Omanis, and places 90% of its purchases in the local market.

items.title: Supply Chain & Vendors
items.text: Register as a supplier and join 1,500 local vendors.

detail.intro: The Supply Chain Management Unit handles orders from vendors and runs vendor registration.
body: Galfar wants reliable, quality-conscious vendors who supply goods and services in the required quality and quantity and keep their delivery promises, so they can take part in its tenders.
Vendors register through Galfar's Supply Chain Portal at gecs.galfar.com.
points: 97% local purchase (NRS) of total purchase order value
7% SMEs of total purchase order value

items.title: Social Responsibility
items.text: Iftar campaigns, blood drives, olive trees and community events.

detail.intro: Galfar's CSR work rests on three pillars: social and community development, youth development and women's empowerment, and environmental preservation.
body: Iftar campaigns distribute food packs to communities in the governorates where Galfar projects run. Blood donation campaigns support community health. Galfar's sponsorship of the Musandam carnival supported SMEs and local tourism in the governorate.
Galfar sponsors educational workshops and mentorship for young professionals and women, and supports environmental work such as planting olive trees and clean-up campaigns.

items.title: Investor Relations
items.text: Listed on the Muscat Stock Exchange since 2007. Annual and ESG reports.

detail.intro: Galfar Engineering & Contracting SAOG has been a public joint stock company on the Muscat Stock Exchange since 2007 (ticker GECS).
body: Annual reports for 2021 to 2025 and ESG reports for 2024 and 2025 are published on galfar.com. Financial performance is shown on the MSX snapshot page.

For 2023 Galfar reported parent company revenue of RO 238.565 million (RO 166.120 million in 2022) and group revenue of RO 250.009 million. On 30 June 2024 its order book stood at RO 816 million, against RO 644 million a year earlier.

catalogue.title: Projects
catalogue.intro: Roads, plants, hospitals, harbours and water networks, from Galfar's iconic projects and recent awards.
catalogue.note: Project facts as published on galfar.com (read 12 Oct 2026). Values are contract values at award.

items.title: Yibal Khuff
items.text: A new central processing facility in the Yibal Khuff area for Petroleum Development Oman.
body: Construction of a new Central Processing Facility in the Yibal Khuff area, covering civil, mechanical, electrical and instrumentation works.
Galfar describes Yibal Khuff, completed in 2021, as its most technically complex project. The plant handles oil and gas separation and processing, and sulphur recovery.

items.title: EPC Harweel Cluster
items.text: Engineering, procurement, construction and commissioning of the Phase 2 facilities.
body: The project covers the engineering, procurement, construction and commissioning of Phase 2 facilities: oil and gas separators, booster compressor, condensate stabiliser unit, gas sweetening unit, dehydration units, injection compressor and gas conditioning unit.
It also includes export oil storage and pumping, pipelines, trunk lines and flow lines, manifold stations and well hook-ups, and the electrical infrastructure.

items.title: Gas Gathering System, Block 61 Khazzan
items.text: About 192 km of duplex stainless steel underground gas pipeline in 30 lines.
body: Construction and installation of the Gas Gathering System (I and II): approximately 192 km of DSS underground gas pipeline for Block 61 Khazzan, a total of 30 lines including main headers and sub-headers.
Above-ground installation work included 3.3 kV power cables laid along the pipeline in a separate 200 km trench, communication backbone nodes and metal-clad distribution substations.

items.title: Qarn Alam Off-Plot Mechanical Contract
items.text: Flow lines, pipelines, well hook-ups and manifolds for PDO at Qarn Alam.
body: The contract provides engineering, sourcing and logistics, construction, pre-commissioning and commissioning, commissioning assistance and management services.

Mechanical scope covers flow line and pipeline design and construction (new and replacement), well hook-up design and construction, HPG well hook-ups and flow lines, hoist preparation (un-hook and re-hook) for oil and gas, and MSV and manifold design and construction.
In February 2024 Galfar announced a five-year contract of about RO 100 million for project delivery services on PDO's Qarn Alam project.

items.title: Oxy Blocks 53 & 72 civil works
items.text: A five-year call-off contract for civil works services for Occidental Oman.
body: Occidental Oman awarded Galfar the service contract for civil works services for Blocks 53 and 72. The contract was accepted by both parties on 25 July 2024.
Galfar estimates the call-off value at about RO 18.5 million over five years from 1 October 2024, with a two-year extension option worth an estimated RO 6.5 million more.

items.title: Muscat Expressway
items.text: A 54 km three-lane expressway from Qurm to Al Naseem.
body: Muscat Expressway (54 km) starts from Qurm in Muscat and passes through Madinat Qaboos, Al Khuwair, Boushar, Al Ansab, Ghala, Airport Heights, Seeb, Al Khoud, Mabela, Rusayl and Halban towards Al Naseem, where it links with the Batinah Expressway.

items.title: Rusayl–Bidbid Road Expansion
items.text: Third and fourth lanes over 27 km, opened to traffic in March 2024.
body: The project adds third and fourth lanes over 27 km, from the Rusayl–Nizwa Interchange on the Muscat Expressway to the Al Sharqiya Expressway Interchange in Bidbid.

It includes service roads, pedestrian crossings, wider valley bridges such as the Wadi Al Jifnain and Wadi Fanja bridges, two new intersections on the Ghala and Al Sih Al Ahmar roads, wider Fanja and Bidbid interchanges, a new bridge in the Wadi Al Dabun area and box culverts for rainwater.
The Ministry of Transport, Communications and Information Technology opened the road in March 2024.

specs.label: Client
specs.value: Ministry of Transport, Communications and IT

items.title: Bousher–Amerat Road
items.text: A 14.5 km mountain road that halved the drive from Amerat to Bousher.
body: Design and construction of the Bousher–Al Amerat road: 14.5 km of mountainous road, a two-lane dual carriageway between Al Amerat and Bousher.

The road starts at Muscat Expressway Interchange No. 5 in Bousher and ends at Al Mahaj roundabout in Al Amerat. It cut the distance from Amerat to Bousher by half and considerably reduced congestion in Wadi Adai.

items.title: Hasik–Shuwaymiyah Road
items.text: About 94 km of road through mountains in Dhofar that had no access before.
body: The Hasik–Shuwaymiyah road connects Hasik and Shuwaymiyah in the north-eastern part of the Governorate of Dhofar. It is a 7 m wide single carriageway, about 94 km long.
Seven kilometres near Hasik and 20 km near Ash Shuwaymiyah lie on flat ground. The rest runs through mountains of various heights that had no access.

specs.label: Client
specs.value: Ministry of Transport, Communications and IT

items.title: Batinah Expressway
items.text: 46.2 km of divided dual four-lane expressway.
body: Galfar built Batinah Expressway packages 1 and 3. The package listed on galfar.com covers the construction of a divided dual four-lane expressway, 46.20 km long, and the superstructure for the structures needed to open the carriageway.

specs.label: Client
specs.value: Ministry of Transport, Communications and IT

items.title: Al Ansab–Al Jifnain Road Dualisation
items.text: A RO 53 million road widening with bridges and underpasses for Muscat Municipality.
body: Muscat Municipality awarded Galfar the RO 53 million Al Ansab–Al Jifnain Road Dualisation project, with a 30-month execution period plus 120 days of mobilisation.

The existing two-lane road is widened to three lanes in each direction, with bridges and underpasses replacing roundabouts. The road links the Governorate of Muscat with Al Dakhiliyah and North Al Sharqiyah.

items.title: Abu Dhabi–Suhar Railway
items.text: A joint venture civil contract worth RO 521 million from Hafeet Rail.
body: Oman–Etihad Rail (Hafeet Rail) awarded a joint venture including Galfar a contract worth RO 521 million (about US$1.4 billion) to build the Abu Dhabi–Suhar railway network.
The Omani–UAE consortium is led by Trojan Construction Group of the UAE and Galfar of Oman. Galfar called it a strategic step into railway projects.

items.title: Salalah International Airport
items.text: Airside and landside works for the new Salalah International Airport.
body: Development of Salalah International Airport: taxiways and aprons with airfield lighting, landside roads and bridges, airside roads with perimeter security fencing, air quality and noise monitoring, storm water drainage, landscaping with irrigation and the landside traffic management system.
Galfar executed the airside works as a joint venture partner.

specs.label: Client
specs.value: Ministry of Transport, Communications and IT

items.title: Duqm Fishery Port
items.text: A fishery harbour on the Al Wusta coast, listed among Galfar's iconic projects.
body: Galfar lists Duqm Fishery Port among the iconic projects it has delivered. Its Infrastructure Unit builds ports, commercial harbours and fishing harbours along Oman's coast.

items.title: Grand Blue City marine works
items.text: Marine works for a seafront community at Al Sawadi, South Al Batinah.
body: Galfar was awarded the construction of marine works at Grand Blue City in Al Sawadi, South Al Batinah. The letter of award was approved by both parties on 23 June 2024.

The project is valued at RO 12 million with an execution period of 24 months. The development will include villas, lagoon villas, a five-star hotel, serviced apartments and 270 residential apartments along the Al Sawadi seafront.

items.title: Medical City for Military and Security Services
items.text: A 458-bed hospital with about 172,785 m² of programme space.
body: Contract A covers the construction and commissioning of a main hospital building and associated ancillary buildings with all external works.
The hospital will accommodate 458 beds and approximately 172,785 m² of programme space, with three basement levels.

items.title: Bank Muscat Headquarters
items.text: Services works for a 36,000 m² head office, energy centre and car park.
body: Services works for the main office building, the energy centre building and external car parking.
The main office building has a total built-up area of 36,000 m²: basement, ground floor and four upper floors. The basement footprint of about 5,000 m² is mainly used for services.

specs.label: Client
specs.value: Bank Civil Service Employees Pension Fund

items.title: Al Ansab Sewage Treatment Plant
items.text: Oman's first membrane bioreactor plant, 52,500 m³ a day.
body: Supply, detailed engineering, construction, installation, testing and commissioning of a 52,500 m³/day extended aeration treatment complex with MBR technology, part of the Muscat wastewater scheme.

Scope included plot preparation, process RCC tanks and structures, non-process buildings, process equipment and piping, services, electrical supply and external roads and paving. Galfar describes it as Oman's first plant of its kind.

items.title: Raysut Water Reclamation Plant expansion
items.text: Phase III (Stage I) expansion for Nama Dhofar Services, RO 35 million.
body: Nama Dhofar Services Company awarded Galfar the Expansion of Raysut Water Reclamation Plants, Phase III (Stage I).
The project is valued at RO 35 million with an execution period of 36 months from commencement.

items.title: Dhahirah water distribution networks
items.text: Design and build of networks for Ibri, Yanqul and Dank, about RO 117 million.
body: Nama Water Services awarded Galfar the design and build tender for water distribution networks in the wilayats of Ibri, Yanqul and Dank in Al Dhahirah Governorate, package 1.
The project is valued at about RO 117 million with an execution period of 44 months from commencement.

highlights.title: Sectors
highlights.intro: The kinds of work behind Galfar's 1,000+ projects, as described by its units.

items.title: Marine & harbours
items.text: Ports, commercial harbours and fishing harbours along Oman's coast.

detail.intro: Galfar's Infrastructure Unit has built ports, commercial harbours and fishing harbours along Oman's coastline.
body: Duqm Fishery Port is listed among Galfar's iconic projects. In June 2024 Galfar was awarded RO 12 million of marine works for Grand Blue City on the Al Sawadi seafront.

items.title: Airports
items.text: Airside works at Salalah, PDO airfields, Ras Al Hadd and Muscat.

detail.intro: Galfar has built several airports in Oman.
body: It executed all airside works at Salalah International Airport as a joint venture partner, and built airports for Petroleum Development Oman so oil fields have all-weather, round-the-clock air operations.
Other work includes the airside facilities at Ras Al Hadd Airport for the Ministry of Transport and the rehabilitation of the old Muscat International Airport.

items.title: Bridges & tunnels
items.text: The highest stabilised walls and longest underpass tunnels in Oman.

detail.intro: Galfar's roads include the highest mechanically stabilised walls and the longest underpass tunnels in Oman.
body: Recent work includes widened valley bridges on the Rusayl–Bidbid road, such as the Wadi Al Jifnain and Wadi Fanja bridges, and bridges and underpasses replacing roundabouts on the Al Ansab–Al Jifnain road.

items.title: Earthworks
items.text: Excavation, backfill and reclamation with Galfar's own heavy fleet.

detail.intro: With its fleet of heavy earthmoving equipment, Galfar's Infrastructure Unit handles excavation, backfill and reclamation at scale.
body: Projects include backfilling for Muscat International Airport and ground levelling for the refinery complex in Duqm.

items.title: Pipelines & flowlines
items.text: More than 8,000 km laid, from wellhead to gathering station.

detail.intro: Galfar's Energy & Industrial Unit has built more than 8,000 km of flowlines and pipelines of different diameters and materials, above and below ground.
body: Its service contracts run from wellhead hook-up to delivery into gathering stations, for Petroleum Development Oman, OQ, BP, Occidental Oman, Daleel and others.

items.title: Power transmission
items.text: Transmission systems from 11 kV to 132 kV.

detail.intro: Galfar has designed and built power transmission systems from 11 kV to 132 kV and can deliver power generation facilities.
body: Its energy work also covers DCS and SCADA control facilities and blast-proof buildings in the oil and gas sector.

items.title: Hospitals
items.text: From Ibri, Nizwa and Sur to the National Heart Centre.

detail.intro: Galfar's Civil & Environmental Unit started in healthcare with the Ibri, Nizwa and Sur general hospitals.
body: The Nizwa hospital included mechanical, electrical, plumbing and HVAC work, which led to larger projects: the Salalah Extended Health Centre, the National Heart Centre at the Royal Hospital, an Accident, Emergency and Burns unit and the Salalah Cardiac Centre, followed by operation and maintenance.
The unit is now building the 458-bed Medical City for Military and Security Services for the Royal Oman Police.
points: Medical City for Military and Security Services

items.title: Hotels & landmarks
items.text: Palaces, monuments, stadiums and turnkey hotels across Oman.

detail.intro: As Galfar's first operating unit, Civil & Environmental has built palaces, commercial buildings, housing, schools, monuments, religious buildings, stadiums and residences.
body: It has built several hotels on a turnkey basis across Oman, and guest complexes, offices, border posts and utility buildings for the Royal Court Affairs and other authorities.

items.title: Fabrication
items.text: Structural steel and alloy piping from the Nizwa Industrial Facility.

detail.intro: The Nizwa Industrial Facility, established in 2006, fabricates for Galfar projects and third-party clients.
body: It runs structural fabrication, CS/LTCS and SS/DSS/SDSS/alloy piping fabrication, plate rolling, and blasting, coating and painting. Galfar also runs a carpentry workshop, a waterproofing and coating complex and scaffolding and formwork installations.

news.title: Galfar secures RO117mn contract from Nama Water Services
news.summary: A design and build contract for water distribution networks in Ibri, Yanqul and Dank, with a 44-month execution period.
body: Nama Water Services has awarded Galfar a contract worth about RO 117 million for the construction of water distribution networks in Al Dhahirah Governorate.

The design and build tender covers the wilayats of Ibri, Yanqul and Dank, package 1, with an execution period of 44 months from commencement. Galfar said the award strengthens its order book and its share of water sector projects.

It was the third major contract Galfar secured in less than a month, after the Raysut water reclamation plant expansion (about RO 35 million) and a five-year service contract from Occidental Oman (about RO 18.5 million).

As of 30 June 2024 Galfar's order book reached RO 816 million, compared with RO 644 million a year earlier, after new awards totalling RO 279 million. In the first half of 2024 the parent company's revenue rose 10.8% to RO 128.9 million, with a net profit of RO 0.86 million.

news.title: Galfar wins RO18.5mn contract from Oxy
news.summary: A five-year civil works service contract for Blocks 53 and 72, with a two-year extension option.
body: Occidental Oman has awarded Galfar a five-year service contract for civil works services for Blocks 53 and 72. The contract was accepted by both parties on 25 July.
Galfar estimates the call-off contract at about RO 18.5 million, with an execution period of five years from 1 October 2024. A two-year extension, if agreed, would add an estimated RO 6.5 million.
Galfar noted that the value may change with the services required. The company said the award supports its order book and its share of energy and industry projects.

news.title: Galfar wins RO35 million contract
news.summary: Nama Dhofar Services awards the expansion of the Raysut Water Reclamation Plants, Phase III (Stage I).
body: Galfar has received a tender worth RO 35 million from Nama Dhofar Services Company for the Expansion of Raysut Water Reclamation Plants, Phase III (Stage I).
The project has an execution period of 36 months from commencement. Galfar said the award will add to its order book and sustain its share of the wastewater sector.

news.title: Galfar awarded tender for marine works at Grand Blue City
news.summary: RO 12 million of marine works on the Al Sawadi seafront in South Al Batinah.
body: Galfar has been awarded the construction of marine works at Grand Blue City in Al Sawadi, South Al Batinah. The letter of award was approved by both parties on 23 June 2024.
The project is valued at RO 12 million, with an execution period of 24 months from commencement.
The development will include luxury villas, lagoon villas, a five-star hotel, serviced apartments and 270 residential apartments along the Al Sawadi seafront.

news.title: Galfar secures major rail contract, poised for infra diversification
news.summary: Hafeet Rail awards a Galfar joint venture RO 521 million to build the Abu Dhabi–Suhar railway.
body: Oman–Etihad Rail (Hafeet Rail) has awarded a joint venture including Galfar a contract worth RO 521 million (about US$1.4 billion) to build the Abu Dhabi–Suhar railway network, Galfar said in a filing to the Muscat Stock Exchange.
The Omani–UAE consortium is led by Trojan Construction Group of the UAE and Galfar of Oman. The award was announced during the state visit of His Majesty Sultan Haitham bin Tarik to the UAE.
Galfar said the win strengthens its order book and positions the company for a strategic move into railway projects.

news.title: Rusayl–Bidbid road expansion project opens for traffic
news.summary: 27 km of third and fourth lanes from the Rusayl–Nizwa Interchange to Bidbid are open.
body: The Ministry of Transport, Communications and Information Technology has opened the Rusayl–Bidbid Road Expansion Project, which adds third and fourth lanes over 27 km from the Rusayl–Nizwa Interchange on the Muscat Expressway to the Al Sharqiya Expressway Interchange in Bidbid.

Service roads and pedestrian crossings connect the communities on both sides. Valley bridges such as the Wadi Al Jifnain and Wadi Fanja bridges were widened, two intersections were built on the Ghala and Al Sih Al Ahmar roads, the Fanja and Bidbid interchanges were widened and a new bridge was built in the Wadi Al Dabun area.
Box culverts drain rainwater, and lighting, concrete and metal barriers, signs and road markings were installed.

news.title: Galfar secures RO 100 million contract for PDO's Qarn Alam project
news.summary: A five-year project delivery services contract for Petroleum Development Oman.
body: Galfar has been awarded a five-year contract worth about RO 100 million for project delivery services on Petroleum Development Oman's Qarn Alam project. The letter of award was accepted by both parties on 30 January 2024.

In unaudited results for 2023, Galfar recorded parent company revenue of RO 238.565 million, up from RO 166.120 million a year earlier. Group revenue totalled RO 250.009 million, up from RO 177.621 million in 2022.

news.title: RO 53M contract for Al Ansab – Al Jifnain road dualisation awarded
news.summary: Muscat Municipality awards a 30-month road widening with bridges and underpasses.
body: Galfar has won the RO 53 million Al Ansab–Al Jifnain Road Dualisation Project from Muscat Municipality, with a 30-month execution period plus 120 days of mobilisation.

The two-lane road will be widened to three lanes in each direction, with bridges and underpasses replacing the roundabouts. The project is part of the development package for the Governorate of Muscat in the 2021–2025 five-year plan.
It will improve movement between Muscat and the governorates of Al Dakhiliyah and North Al Sharqiyah.

faq.a: Galfar was established in 1972. Its first project was a villa for the Wali of Sur, and it obtained its commercial registration in 1975.
Yes. Galfar Engineering & Contracting SAOG has been listed on the Muscat Stock Exchange since 2007 under the ticker GECS, with more than 4,000 shareholders.

faq.q: What kind of projects does Galfar build?
faq.a: Three business units cover oil and gas, industrial and power projects; roads, bridges, airports, ports, dams, rail and water networks; and buildings, MEP and wastewater plants, including operation and maintenance.

faq.q: How do I register as a supplier?
faq.a: Vendors register through Galfar's Supply Chain Portal at gecs.galfar.com. More than 1,500 local vendors and suppliers are registered.

faq.q: How do I apply for a job at Galfar?
faq.a: Open roles are listed on Galfar's careers portal at galfar.zohorecruit.com.

faq.q: Where can I find the annual reports?
faq.a: Annual reports for 2021 to 2025 and ESG reports for 2024 and 2025 are published on the Investor Inquiries and Publications pages of galfar.com.

faq.q: Which standards is Galfar certified to?
faq.a: Galfar's QHSSE management system is certified to ISO 9001, ISO/TS 29001, ISO 14001 and ISO 45001.
Call the head office on +968 2452 5000 or email info@galfar.com. The postal address is Post Box 533, Muscat, Postal Code 100, Sultanate of Oman.

Pipelines: the overview and unit text say 8,000+ km, the Energy & Industrial page header says over 10,000 km. The site uses 8,000+.
Local purchasing: ICV says 90% of purchases are local, Supply Chain says 97% local purchase (NRS). Both shown in their context.
Founding year: galfar.com says 1972; the rail news item says 1971. The site uses 1972. The home page still says 52 years' experience.
Galfar's site spells Qarn Alam as 'Qarn Alalm' and calls the company 'Gulf Engineering and Contracting' in the Grand Blue City item (value written R012 million). Corrected silently.
Raysut news is dated 30 June 2024 but says the letter of award was accepted on 25 July 2024 (announced elsewhere as 30 July). Check the date.
Qarn Alam: the Off-Plot Mechanical Contract (unit page) and the RO 100 million project delivery services contract (Feb 2024 news) are shown on one project page. Confirm they are the same contract.
Gas Gathering System, Block 61 Khazzan: galfar.com lists the client as PDO (Block 61 Khazzan is operated by BP). Confirm the client.
Status of 2023–2024 awards (Al Ansab–Al Jifnain, Raysut, Dhahirah, Oxy, Grand Blue City, Hafeet Rail) is shown as 'Awarded' only. Current progress is not published.

Nizwa and Khazain facility addresses and phone numbers are not published; their map pins sit on the town centres (Nizwa, Barka), not the sites; the head office number is shown. Head office coordinates come from the plus code H9F4+F29 in the contact map.

Client names come from the logo wall on galfar.com; one emblem (gold crest) could not be identified and is left out.
